title: KV shadow occupancy profiling: bank-aware stripe throttling walkthrough
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working walkthrough of a set of exploratory runs aimed at isolating a recurring tail-latency / throughput collapse that correlates with KV cache bank hotspots during mixed-seqlen workloads. Goal: identify whether the dominant limiter is (A) bank/channel saturation on the host <-> gpu DMA path, (B) NVMe pageback amplification from eviction storms, or (C) internal CPU-side contention in the cache manager (locks/GC).

Why this is different from recent kv experiments:
- Instead of focusing on global reuse rates, this notebook samples per-bank occupancy (shadow occupancy) over time and correlates to per-request memory channel utilization and PCIe counters.
- Introduces an experiment to artificially stripe eviction work across banks (bank-aware stripe throttling) and measures impact on P95/P99 and aggregate throughput.

High-level hypothesis:
1) Mixed seqlen workloads create nonuniform hotsets that concentrate KV hits on a small set of banks, causing momentary memory channel saturation and long DMA latencies for spill/prefetch paths.
2) That saturation triggers allocator/backpressure interactions in our cache coordinator which then batch-evict pages, causing NVMe pageback that amplifies latency.
3) Smoothing eviction across banks should reduce transient stalls and improve tail latency with minimal cost to aggregate reuse.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Workloads: short-only (S), long-only (L), mixed (70%S/30%L by request count), bursty-mixed (periodic long spikes).
- Config knobs: eviction-strategy={lru, bank-aware-round-robin}, eviction-throttle-ms={0,2,10}, prefetch={on,off}, kv-ttl-ms={0,500,2000}.
- Metrics collected: per-bank occupancy (samples/ms), PCIe read/write throughput (samples/sec), NVMe qdepth, host DRAM channel utilization (perf), GPU DMA latency histogram, request P50/P95/P99 latency, reuse_rate_by_request_bucket.

Platform / repro details:
- Node: 4x A100-40GB (simulated HBM pressure via synthetic requests), host: 2x 32-core AMD, 512GB DRAM, NVMe Samsung PM1733 (3.5 GB/s measured), OS kernel 5.15 custom perf hooks enabled.
- Build: serving-runtime@main + kv-shadow-instrumentation branch (PR 879). Kernel perf counters sampled at 200Hz, per-request tracing via eBPF for DMA start/end.
- Synthetic trace generator: trace-gen v0.9 (attached), with realistic KV key distribution (Zipfian s=1.05) and seqlen distributions matching customer-prod traces.

Observations (selected runs):
1) Mixed workload, baseline LRU, no throttle:
   - Aggregate throughput: 26k req/s
   - P95: 24ms, P99: 210ms (long tail)
   - Shadow occupancy: top 10% of banks held 62% of resident set during spikes
   - Host DRAM channel utilization: top channel ~92% utilization spike for 120ms windows
   - NVMe qdepth: spikes to 64+ and observed avg pageback latency 9ms -> triggers request stalls
   - Reuse rate (per-request): short requests show reuse 78%, long requests 11%
   - Annotated note: these numbers match the customer report pattern (JIRA-RI-1124).

2) Mixed workload, bank-aware-round-robin eviction, throttle 2ms:
   - Aggregate throughput: 25.1k req/s (−3.5%)
   - P95: 12ms, P99: 42ms (substantial tail improvement)
   - Shadow occupancy: top 10% banks down to 28% during spikes (much smoother)
   - DRAM channel utilization: peak channel 56% in same windows; more evenly distributed
   - NVMe qdepth: peaks lower (avg 18) and pageback latency reduced to 3.2ms
   - Reuse rate: short requests 76%, long 10% (minor change)
   - CPU contention: small increase (2 cores bumped to 60% usage) due to stripe coordinator work

3) Bursty-mixed (periodic long spikes), no prefetch, bank-aware RR + 10ms throttle:
   - Throughput: 21.5k req/s (expected drop due to higher throttle)
   - P95/P99: 9ms / 16ms (very stable tail)
   - NVMe pageback almost eliminated during spikes (qdepth <= 6)
   - Comment: aggressive throttle hurts steady throughput but eliminates pageback amplification — good option for strict SLOs.

Micro-profiling hints (from eBPF traces and perf):
- DMA latency distribution shows bimodal peaks during eviction storms: ~40–60us normal, and ~250–500us when channel saturated.
- The cache coordinator lock (coordinator::eviction_lock) shows contended wait spikes correlated with NVMe qdepth rise. Stack sampling often points to "schedule()" after submit_pageback().
- PCIe counter correlation: when bank 3 is hot, PCIe read_bytes/sec from that GPU region jump 3–4x compared to baseline; sustained >600MB/s on that lane correlates to ±200us latency increase per DMA op.

Quick diagrams (verbal):
- Time series: shadow-occupancy(top10banks) -> DRAM channel util -> NVMe qdepth -> p99 latency show causal alignment within 50–150ms windows.

Actionable next steps and proposed mitigations:
1) Ship a low-risk bank-aware eviction mode behind a feature flag (bank-aware-eviction=true). Default to off. (PR 879 has prototype)
2) Implement a coordinator-side evict-throttle window to smooth eviction bursts (configurable ms). Add metric: eviction_batches/sec.
3) Add a lightweight per-bank token-bucket for prefetch/evict IO submissions to bound PCIe/HOST channel injection. This should be kernel-counter-informed.
4) For customer SLOs where tail is critical, recommend aggressive throttle + prewarm for long-request spikes; provide a deployment recipe in Console Optimize.
5) Follow-up profiling: instrument NVMe driver qdepth attribution per-client to confirm cross-tenant amplification risk (ticket: JIRA-RI-1137).

Open questions / risks:
- Is the host DRAM channel saturation primarily caused by DMA scheduling on GPU or by contiguous page layout causing a single-channel hotness? Need to run hw-topology-aware allocator experiment.
- Bank-aware eviction increases CPU-side work — at what scale (multi-GPU nodes) will coordinator become a bottleneck? We saw small CPU uptick; need scale test with 64k concurrent requests.
- Potential fairness issues: round-robin stripe may disadvantage very-hot keys — consider weighted stripe using per-key hotness estimate.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add sampling-based per-request key->bank mapping export in telemetry (light sampling, 1/1000) to check in prod traces.
- Re-run mixed workload with prefetch=on + bank-aware RR + throttle=2ms but with larger resident set (2x) to validate reuse change.
- Draft a short runbook: when pageback latency > 5ms, turn on bank-aware throttling + set eviction-throttle-ms=2.
- Sync with infra team about enabling per-channel perf counters on cloud instances (ask: can we get PCIe lane specific counters?).

Appendix: quick commands used (for reproducibility):
- start perf collector: perf record -F 200 -a -g -- sleep 300 (with eBPF capture)
- nvme stats: nvme-cli get-feature / sysfs qdepth; iostat -x 1
- trace generator: ./trace-gen --profile mixed70-30.zipf --duration 600 --out /tmp/run-2025-07-02
- kv shadow sampler: ./kv-shadow-sampler --sample-ms 5 --out /tmp/shadow-2025-07-02.csv

If we want to iterate: prioritize the bank-aware token-bucket + low-latency throttle and test on customer-like traffic. I'm going to add a short PR description and a recommended default config for the feature-flag.

End of walkthrough.
